Ecuador’s Sweeping Import Tariffs Disrupt Supply Chains and Raise Prices

QUITO, June 20 — Ecuador’s newly enacted broad import tariffs are sending ripples through the economy, leading to price hikes and supply shortages across a range of products, industry groups and analysts said Thursday.

The measure, in place since last week, imposes a 35% surcharge on most imported goods in an effort to shore up Ecuador’s weakening balance of payments and protect local industry. The government said the tariffs will remain “until further notice,” as foreign reserves remain under pressure.

“We had to act to prevent further currency outflows and support domestic producers,” Economy Minister Luis Carrasco told reporters. “These are temporary measures, but essential under the current circumstances.”

The tariffs, which apply to consumer electronics, auto parts, textiles, processed foods and more, have led to immediate disruptions. Importers report bottlenecks at ports as customs procedures slow, and some retailers say inventories are already running low. Street vendors in Guayaquil and Quito cited sharp price increases for items such as mobile phones, kitchen appliances and imported packaged foods.

“Since the tariffs started, our costs have jumped by at least 30%,” said Ana Delgado, manager of the retail chain Casa Nueva. “Customers are frustrated, and we’re struggling to restock.”

The National Chamber of Commerce warned that prolonged restrictions could “lead to layoffs and business closures,” while the Federation of Small Exporters voiced concern about potential retaliation from trade partners.

Economist Javier Ponce of the Quito Policy Institute said, “While these tariffs may help the trade balance in the short term, they risk fueling inflation and harming consumers.”

Government officials said they are monitoring the situation and will review the measures in the coming weeks. In the meantime, many Ecuadorians continue to face rising costs and uncertain supply of everyday goods.
